metadata.title: The analytical value of non-probability samples in the context of TALIS (EN)

extraction.outcome_summary: The paper reviewed established uses of non-probability samples in comparative, cross-national survey contexts and assessed their policy relevance. It concluded that non-probability samples are generally unfit for TALIS’s main purposes because they can substantially reduce accuracy and do not support design-based uncertainty quantification. However, it argued that non-probability approaches could be useful in specific TALIS-related scenarios, such as complementary longitudinal modules, field-trial development phases, and exploratory scoping surveys, especially when risks are mitigated through theoretically grounded confounders, controlled sampling procedures, post hoc adjustments, and transparent reporting.
